verdict.for_whom: You should buy this if you have a reliable group of friends to tackle chaotic co-op challenges with, but skip it if you prefer playing alone or dislike games that require repetitive grinding to unlock gear.

distortion_flags.sentence: User satisfaction starts low due to initial technical barriers, climbs significantly as squad gameplay clicks, and then drops again among long-term players frustrated by endgame grinding and persistent bugs.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Technical hurdles dominate early on, with system crashes, matchmaking issues, and an unskippable cinematic. Playing alone is described as overly difficult, with the game proving far better when played alongside companions.

This game doesn't work properly on my damn computer, just look at my screenshots.
Fix your game faster you lazy bums. Video driver crashes every 10 minutes is a fking unacceptable for a game of it budget.

claims.claim: Reviewers report connection and matchmaking errors, such as failing to join lobbies, connection time-outs, and issues with peer-to-peer connectivity.

citations.review_text:
600k reviews and its peer to peer connection

imagine space x gathering trillions of dollars and not launching a single rocket

Requested a refund after 1.6 hours.

I never got to experience the actual game because every attempt to join a public lobby ended with "Failed to join lobby" or "Connection timed out." Quickplay also searched for several minutes without finding a match. I tried the common fixes but nothing worked. The main reason I bought this was for the multiplayer experience but I ended up trying just to get in a match with other randoms for the entire playtime which is ridiculous, and it just said this same error timed out again and again even though my network was fine. My job is to play not to go around and troubleshoot finding YT tutorials how to disable something just to run a game.
After searching online, I found many players reporting the same issue over the years and still hasn't been fixed as of 3/7/26 . If you're experiencing this too, please upvote this review so the developers can see how widespread it is.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention an unskippable PlayStation cinematic movie that plays upon launching the game.

citations.review_text:
Genuinely the worst shooter game I have ever played.

First of all, there is an UNSKIPPABLE PlayStation cinematic movie that plays every single time you launch the game. They are literally forcing us to worship the enemy just to even play.

Let us also never forget the fiasco of almost forcing us to use a PSN account, and the Discord moderation (power grab) incident.

As for gameplay itself: the reload system is garbage, the camera movement is bugged, and this game in general is a hodgepodge of theft from other, BETTER shooter games.

Simply just play Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine II. That is the quintessential third-person racism shooter. I would rather support them instead of this garbage that rigged the awards shows only because it was not allowed on Xbox for over a year.

I love this game as much as I love drinking Sojū, but I play on Xbox. I'm trying to switch to PC, and I have no choice but to start from scratch. I hope that, in the future, AH will add cross-progression between Xbox and PC, or at least allow players to link a PlayStation account with an Xbox account.

If you're hoping to keep your progress when moving from Xbox to PC, I don't recommend buying the game.

If you don't mind starting over from zero, then go ahead and buy it, it´s a great game.

cohorts.summary: The experience is vastly better with companions or random squads than playing alone, though system freezes and crashes continue to disrupt sessions. The lack of cross-progression is noted, and the highest difficulty settings spark debate, with feedback pointing to endless enemy spawns that make missions feel unplayable.

citations.review_text: Cool game where you spread democracy across the galaxy. No cross-progression however. Very bummed because of this.

Im here switching from playstation to pc and my switch is mostly great but i do wish there was some form of cross progression cause i played on playstaion since the realese of the game and im gonna miss the molevolent creek cape it was one of my favorites that and the illuminate cape aswell

claims.claim: Reviewers find solo play less enjoyable or harder compared to playing with friends or random squads.

citations.review_text: Very fun but play with others. Single player isn't as enjoyable. Be paitient with the devs.

Hello and welcome to a review of helldivers 2 . If you can't be bothered to read tldr 7.5/10 like the 3rd best horde game on the market . If i could choose neutral i would .

-the Good-

1) A good gameplay loop , this game is effectively a hybrid between horde and extraction games . 

2) Many varied mission types , from defending a base , to exterminating everything , to rescuing civilians . 

3) Virtually no monetization 

4) this game has no classes but you can have pretty much infinite custom classes with the strategems system .

- the Bad -

1) Price . Even if the game is solid 30 dollars is just insane when you can get games like Deep rock galactic and payday 2 for like 10 and 3 respectively . 

2) Extremely group heavy even for horde standards , to the point that even if you play solo you have to be playing with random squads otherwise you basically can't win in the last 3 difficulties . 

3) There is pretty much no active teamwork in the game besides using different stratagems in the lobby and maybe healing up a teammate . 

4) Balance is just godawful especially in mid/high difficulties , What is the point of vehicles existing at all if you can just call a jetpack twice as often , be physically faster that vehicles and also being able to reach high places where enemies can't hit you ? Whats the point of having different enemy factions if the players can just use the same 4 stratagems for everything and still beat them ?

5) The Developers either have HUGE egos in real life or have the effective IQ of a child with 6 different mental disorders . Imagine the community asking you to not nerf for the 7th time a gun NOBODY used anyways , then saying you won't , then nerf it anyways and don't write in the patch notes that you nerfed in ON PURPOSE and then have people find it out anyways and continue getting clowned on .

- the ugly - 

1) Crashes and random corrupts of the game just happen for no reason . Its not that bad that i would stop playing but it is bad eno…
If you want a game to play with friends this is what to buy though solo can get boring at some points. All over a great game with funny situations throughout.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience computer freezes, crashes, and forced restarts while playing.

citations.review_text:
Bought this game, played and had fun for about 4-5 hours last night.

Boot up the game today - hard freeze and had to power cycle my PC to unfreeze it.

Reinstalled drivers, updated BIOS, disabled XMP, enabled Secure Boot, deleted shader cache, reinstalled VC, did basically every. fix. imaginable - still crashing. This game is so terrible that there's a community tool made to SPECIFICALLY troubleshoot the game because it's so poorly made and so poorly optimized. I had loads of gun during the gameplay itself but the past day has left such a sore taste in my mouth I vow to not touch this game ever again. Save your money and DO NOT BUY THIS GAME.

Between 10 minute to an hour of playing, the game freezes my entire computer, causing it to automatically restart after about 10 seconds. I've tried several fixes and nothing has worked. This game has now crashed my computer 5-6 times. I would be willing to continue attempt further fixes if testing them didn't take up to an hour before violently forcing my pc to restart. It's frankly ridiculous to expect anyone to put up with this. The 3 friends I'm trying to play with have similar or worse hardware and experience no crashes. What the hell man.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: The loop begins to feel repetitive after extensive play, compounded by a lack of unique stats on armor and disappointing mission rewards. Access to warbonds also draws criticism, with feedback highlighting that premium content requires either real money or tedious grinding.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game becomes repetitive after playing for dozens of hours.

citations.review_text:
Helldivers 2 gameplay mostly consists of you and your squad deploying to different planets to complete operations that have the purpose of winning the galactic war and protecting Super Earth.

 You can play alone but its even better if you play with friends or with strangers in voice chat, in particular in higher difficulty missions where things get chaotic, which usually leads to insane moments where you somehow make it out alive out of a situation that looked impossible to survive. In higher difficulties it is almost impossible to complete operations by yourself, often needing teammates that are able to coordinate with you to complete the objectives. 

 The game also features a few currencies, some to upgrade your destroyers capability, others to buy stratagems, outfits and other items.

 The different factions, different creatures such as bile titans and hulks, and planets provide variety in terms of gameplay, difficulty or visuals , some planets are stunning visually, some creatures are immune to certain weapons, different objectives require different strategies. Another factor that helps in gameplay variety is the huge collection of stratagems, where you have support weapons, orbital or eagle strikes and turrets or sentries, this also provides different possibilities when facing a certain mission.

The only problem is that after several missions, even though there are different factions planets and operations, it might get repetitive, and it gets worse if you play to farm items such as samples, which is not bad, but it usually leads to very repetitive gameplay, so ideally don't stress about quickly getting everything max level and getting game items and focus more on enjoying the gameplay. 

 When it comes to performance, my specs are not very strong but i am able to play the game at medium settings with around 60fps, which is acceptable for me, if you have better specs then you are probably fine, if your system is weaker then you should be a bit more careful …
game is good at the start. gets repetitive late game though. still fun with friends.
cool and fun for a bit but it gets so repetetive

I've been wanting to play Helldivers 2 for the longest time and finally got it on the steam summer sale. It runs very well on my PC. The gameplay can get repetitive, but remains fun. I really enjoy playing it with my friends.
beside the fact that developers cannot handle the game it was fun. lack of content after 50 hours.

claims.claim: Reviewers note a lack of progression or meaningful rewards after completing missions, stating that items and armor lack unique stats.

citations.review_text:
I haven't been here for all the drama so I'm just basing this review on my gameplay experience. 

1. It drives me crazy that your loadout doesn't save between rounds. I avoid purchasing new items because I don't want my loadout screen to have a hundred items that I have to sort through before each mission. 

I bought two warbonds with real money and the rest will sit unpurchased because I don't want to have to search through stratagems every mission, they're literally losing money over this.

2. There's not really any incentive to play. You don't really get anything for beating a mission other than some level xp and a few research samples. You can go tens of hours without unlocking anything new, even longer if you're purposefully avoiding useless item unlocks because your loadouts don't save between rounds (see point 1).

The gameplay is actually fun, but the game itself doesn't feel finished.

Game is fun and at first it seems like  u have a lot of stuff to aim for and unlock. Until you realize everything is just cosmetics, specially the armory. Scopes gives no actual benefits. On my 2nd day i was able to reach Super Helldive difficulty and there is no sense of progression cause there is no way to actually improve your weapons/armor. Stats are always the same, All Magazines have the exact same amount of total bullets despite some being depicted as "High Capacity", same deal for armors, no unique stats or passives. Weapons with X armor piercing doesnt really do anything they still get "deflected" by the same armor they say they pierce. If you want to play max difficulty just buy Exo Suit

The warbond system is ass, it's more efficient to work a minimum wage job than farm super credits, that is not hyperbole.

Fun game but 90% of gear is locked behind either a paywall or grinding low level boring missions for hours on end and the devs seem more concerned with the people cheating their grindy freemium currency into their accounts than thinking about why people would feel the need to cheat for it in the first place

i paid $60 for this game near launch, and i loved playing it. i upgraded my graphics card so i could witness 380s drop in glorious 1080p. i roleplayed as an ODST when the HALO warbond dropped, and i had so much mf fun. 

but locking additional content behind a $10-15 paywall, regularly, for months on end? Dude, based of the initial valuation of the game (ratio of $60 to fun had, content, etc), this warbond price point is so f****** disrespectful. This game is just not worth $180 ($60 + 12 warbonds x $10) - up front or long term. It just plain isn't. And it certainty isn't worth it to farm the SC manually. to do the rough numbers:
Lets say you farm 600 SC per hour. 1000 SC = $10 USD, which maps out to $6 of value an hour in SC. This is not guaranteed however, so you end up running between a low of maybe 400 and a high of 600 per hour - call it an average of 500. You're getting paid $5 an hour? to sit on the lowest difficulties and spam missions, insta-quitting once all the POIs are done? anyone who says "just grind for a few hours" does not understand that you can make more money going to work at a US federal minimum wage job for 2 hrs. Compare soul-crushing grinding to just buying it for almost the same amount of time spent - and bruh why tf are you not buying the SC? they set this s*** up like this! so you are incentivized to purchase the SC, which takes you out of the gameplay loop, and makes the warbonds a momentary inconvenience to your wallet and time instead of the result of play!? TF!?!?! have they forgotten they made a game, not a credit card skimmer??

i'd love to hop in and play the over-the-top and action-packed game i played near launch, where things felt fun and new. but what is the point of playing if all the new toys are locked behind $120 worth of "well, just buy the new one real quick and don't think too hard about the long term cost!" disrespectful as hell to shadow-price a game like this. don't get me started on how they downsized warbond content …

this game is so pay to win its not even funny you get almost nothing if you don't do micro transactions you get one warbond progression and thats it in what world do you pay for a game to play it just to haft to pay more to progress and unlock stuff this game had so much potential but they ruined it with pay for this pay for that pay to play period

No matter what positives I had with this game, it just does not deserve your money.

The economy and progression in this game is disgustingly awfull. For the game the main appeal of which is to try to fight through the different levels and enemies with different loadouts, you will slog through the first 20 hours with the same equipment because your earning are ♥♥♥♥, while strugling to even understnad, what is useful and what is not. Next 3 or 4 missions will be spent testing out new weapons after which the realisation hits that the entire game has 3 or 4 usefull primaries and secondaries, and the entre asrenal apart from that is useless trash that exists only to be a waste of your time AND money.

The system of Warbonds is honestly the worst part if this game by far. Do you like your full priced games that demand you to pay for microtransactions to continue to play? No? Well, bad luck, buddy, be ready to waste 20 more hours to farm 20 Supecredits per mission to by another 1000 credit warbond with steaming ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that will gather dust in your inventory because it's can't even kill medium sized enemies. And don't forget that all your currencies (except for the premium microtransaction one) is capped, so you can't even save up your medals (currency that is used to buy items from warbonds) because they are capped at 250. What if you had more but don't have warbond to spend them on? Tough luck buddy, be ready to waste all your medals!

The game is just terminally unfun. The moment anything in this game gets any mileage against enemies, it gets nerfed into the ground, the game demands you to pay for even dare to try to use different equipment, higher difficulties exist only to be annoying and be a waste of your time, bugs are never fixed because fixing them does not bring developers money, and you can't even argue that game has good graphics because you will be blasted by the absurd amount of dust in your face constantly. cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term engagement is hampered by persistent technical instability and crashes. Additionally, the premium warbonds and gear are locked behind time-consuming grinds for credits or direct purchases, which dampens the endgame experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that premium currency and warbonds require significant grinding to acquire or involve paid transactions in a non-free-to-play game.

citations.review_text: Garbage game about battlepasses, without adequate implementation of paid currency being acquired for doing anything except grinding lvl 1 mission with a specific pattern of the map. Pay a fortune for the game - pay once more to use weapons that barely find their use on battlefield.

tldr: A paid game which is pretty fun but uses egregious F2P monetization. Clear potential for greatness, if only it were in better hands.

Sure, I like the gameplay. But SO MUCH of the gear is locked behind premium passes. While you can technically get the premium currency while playing, the rate at which this happens essentially means you'll have no time to play other games if you play normally. Or you'll be spending evenings here and there doing nothing but the lowest most boring difficulty JUST to gather that premium currency efficiently.

Seriously, let's do a quick comparison to Helldivers 1: HD1 has 14 pieces of DLC, the most expensive one being €4.
Helldivers2 has 22 of these warbonds/premium passes at €10+ each (2 of which cost 50% extra and give back €0 instead of the roughly €3 worth of currency the regular ones do), and counting. My primary issue isn't even the difference in quantity, it's the fact that not a single premium pass feels worth the asking price. To me each warbond is offering roughly the same amount of meaningful content as one HD1 DLC, yet they're double the price.

Additionally, HD1 DLC actually goes on sale. To my knowledge HD2 warbonds have never gone on sale, not even a reduction in price for the oldest ones.

There's also been no additions of meaningful progression besides these premium warbonds since (just checking the patch's date here) two years ago, 4th of july 2024. (I'm not counting the gun customization, it's a nice little bonus but it's also quite underbaked and has had no attention since its own implementation. Heck, they don't even properly show the stats that get changed, since the screen claims sway remains the same no matter what).

There's more issues I have with the game (performance, bugginess, stratagem bounce, biome limitations, the meaninglessness of the overarching forced plot from the perspective of a single player, unreliability of actual in-match difficulty when selecting a difficulty) but I can't really bother t…

A $40 game with a free to play monetization model, the only progression is through battle passes and once you complete the first one that's free, you have to pay real money. Some of the best (and most fun) weapons and armor are behind these passes which is extremely frustrating since this is not a free to play game, yet you still have to pay to get them. While Premium currency can be obtained through gameplay the most optimal methods to do so are not only extremely boring, but very time consuming. It can take upwards of seven hours of grinding (with average luck) to get just a single battle pass (called War Bonds), which will only give you back 300 SC for the next purchase.

It's such a shame too since behind this atrocious pay-to-progress model, with some of the worst grinding I've seen in a paid game, is an actually fun co-op shooter. I just can't recommend it because the monetization is so greedy and so intrusive that it can really hinder the actual fun part of the game. Wherein if you want to play with some of the coolest items the game has, you will either need to fork out $10, ($15 for the legendary bonds), or grind out hours and hours of boring SC farming just to get it for free.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from recurring crashes and technical instability.

citations.review_text:
I’m marking Helldivers 2 as "Not Recommended" for now, even though I’ve genuinely enjoyed the game and put a lot of time and effort into it.

When the game is working well, it can be a lot of fun. I’ve been through the highs and lows with Helldivers 2 and tried to stick with it because I really wanted to keep enjoying it. Unfortunately, the current state of the game has made that very difficult. My PC meets, and even exceeds, the required specs, but the game continues to crash repeatedly.

The biggest issue is that updates often feel unfinished, and instead of improving stability, the game feels more unstable over time. It is frustrating as a consumer to invest so much time into a game for entertainment, only for it to become difficult or impossible to enjoy because of crashes, bugs, and ongoing performance issues.

I really hope the developers are able to get the game into a more stable and playable state. I would like to come back to Helldivers 2 someday and enjoy it again, because there is a great game here when it works. But right now, I cannot recommend it because it simply does not feel stable or reliable enough to play.

This is a great game but AH need to work on its stability, crashes so often its unplayable and the game doesn't even detect the crash and thinks its still running so no crash report is sent. Its a great game, if it decides to run.
